item.title: His Crashed Car Was Found But Bryce Was Gone
item.description: Bryce Laspisa vanished in 2013 while driving home from college in California. His SUV was found crashed near Castaic Lake with his phone, wallet and laptop still inside, but there was no sign of Bryce. Despite extensive searches, he remains missing.

item.title: Her Boyfriend Was Convicted 10 Years After She Vanished
item.description: Crystal Rogers disappeared from Bardstown, Kentucky, in 2015, and her car was later found abandoned with her belongings inside. Her body has never been found. In 2025, former boyfriend Brooks Houck was convicted of her murder and later sentenced to life in prison.

item.title: Her Husband Was Wanted For Murder When Police Closed In
item.description: Influencer Alexis Sharkey was found dead beside a Houston road in November 2020, and an autopsy determined she had been strangled. Police later named her husband, Tom Sharkey, as the murder suspect. He died by suicide in 2021 as authorities moved to arrest him.

item.title: He Entered An Underwater Cave And Was Never Found
item.description: Ben McDaniel was last seen entering the underwater cave at Florida’s Vortex Spring in August 2010. Extensive searches reached deep into the cave but found no body or clear evidence of where he went. His disappearance remains unsolved.

item.title: Her Mother Convinced Her She Was Dying Of Cancer
item.description: Seven-year-old Hannah Milbrandt was told she had terminal leukemia, but police discovered her mother, Teresa, had fabricated the illness, shaved Hannah’s head and gave her sleeping pills. Teresa later pleaded guilty to child endangerment and theft and received 6½ years in prison.

item.title: His Death Was Ruled Suicide But His Family Disagreed
item.description: Christian Andreacchio was found dead in a Mississippi apartment in 2014. Authorities and the medical examiner ruled his death a suicide, but his family has long challenged that conclusion. A grand jury later declined to indict two people connected to the case.

item.title: A Night Out Ended With Danroy Henry Shot By Police
item.description: Pace University student Danroy Henry Jr. was fatally shot by a police officer in New York in 2010 after a disturbance he was not involved in. Witness accounts differed over the encounter, and both a grand jury and federal prosecutors declined to bring criminal charges against the officer.

item.title: The Person Who Parked Jennifer Kesse’s Car Was Never Identified
item.description: Jennifer Kesse vanished from Orlando in 2006 after failing to show up for work. Her car was found about a mile from her condo, and surveillance footage captured an unidentified person walking away from it. Twenty years later, Jennifer remains missing and no suspect has been named.
